issues.description: Runtime dependency pin `setuptools<82` leaks a CI workaround into production install_requires.
issues.detail: The shell scripts cap setuptools because mmcv's build path needs pkg_resources. But `core/setup.py` installs `setuptools<82` into every downstream user's environment forever. That's a CI hack stapled onto the package's runtime data structure. Wrong data shape: the constraint belongs in the CI workflow files (where the other two FIXMEs live), not in the library's dependency list.

issues.description: Three near-identical setuptools pins in three files with no single source of truth.
issues.detail: `env_setup.sh`, `setup_mmcv.sh`, and `core/setup.py` each independently assert `setuptools<82` with overlapping FIXME comments pointing at the same upstream issue. When mmcv 3325 is fixed, someone has to remember all three sites. A constant or shared script would let one edit revert the workaround. Small composition opportunity.

issues.description: Silent jump from mmdet 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 buried in a setuptools fix.
issues.detail: The PR title says fix mmengine failure. The diff also bumps mmdet a minor version and switches mmengine from a pinned git SHA to PyPI 0.10.7. These are separate decisions with separate risk surfaces; bundling them under one CI patch makes the change harder to bisect later. Worth a sentence in the commit body.

issues.description: `--no-build-isolation` on mmcv silently couples the install to the host environment.
issues.detail: Using `--no-build-isolation` means mmcv's build now reads whatever setuptools is in the active env. That works because the previous line pins `setuptools<82`, but the coupling is invisible. A short inline comment explaining why isolation is disabled would save the next maintainer a half-hour of archaeology when the constraint is lifted.

review.summary: SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE for the CI scripts: the shell changes are the right shape — pin setuptools, install in order, comment with the upstream issue. The real complaint is data-structure: a CI workaround leaked into `core/setup.py`'s install_requires, which is the wrong place for it. Three independent copies of the same pin with no shared constant invite drift when the upstream fix lands. The mmdet version bump rides along quietly and deserves its own line in the commit message.
